turns.user_message: After the two-pass load is done, what's the best way to validate that all 12,000 donor records came across correctly?
turns.assistant_message: The most reliable validation strategy is a three-layer reconciliation: record count, financial totals, and relationship integrity. Start by comparing the total record count in your new Salesforce org's Contact object against the source CSV row count, then compare the sum of all Opportunity amounts in NPSP against the sum from your legacy system's export. For relationship integrity, run a SOQL query on npsp__Partial_Soft_Credit__c to confirm you have exactly 800 records and that every one has a non-null npsp__Amount__c and a valid Opportunity lookup. Any discrepancy at any layer should halt your go-live until resolved.

turns.user_message: We're also worried about duplicate contacts. Our old system wasn't strict about deduplication, so we suspect there could be several hundred duplicates in those 12,000 records. What tools does NPSP offer for that?
turns.assistant_message: NPSP itself doesn't ship with a standalone dedup engine, but Salesforce's native Duplicate Management feature (available in all editions since the Spring '15 release) works well in conjunction with it. You can configure Duplicate Rules and Matching Rules on the Contact object—the standard 'Standard Contact Duplicate Rule' uses fuzzy matching on first name, last name, and email. For a pre-migration dedup pass on your CSV before you ever load into Salesforce, tools like OpenRefine (free, open-source) or a commercial option like Dedupe.io can cluster likely duplicates using Jaro-Winkler string similarity, which handles common misspellings in donor names. Running the dedup before load is strongly preferable to cleaning up inside Salesforce after the fact.

turns.user_message: That's helpful. One of our data fields is 'preferred_contact_method' with values like Email, Phone, Mail, and Do Not Contact. Is there a standard NPSP field for that, or do we need to create a custom one?
turns.assistant_message: NPSP doesn't have a single out-of-the-box field that exactly mirrors a four-value 'preferred_contact_method' picklist. The closest standard field is the Salesforce Contact object's 'HasOptedOutOfEmail' boolean and the related 'DoNotCall' boolean, but those only cover opt-outs rather than positive preferences. For 'Do Not Contact' you can map to a combination of both booleans set to true, but for Email, Phone, and Mail preferences you'll want to create a custom picklist field—something like Contact.Preferred_Contact_Method__c—so you preserve the full fidelity of your source data. Document that mapping decision in your migration spec so future staff know why the custom field exists.

turns.user_message: Can you help me track down the schedule for the orders pipeline? I need to know exactly when it runs.
turns.assistant_message: The orders pipeline is currently scheduled to run every night at 02:15 UTC. That schedule is defined in the legacy Autosys job named JOB_ORDERS_NIGHTLY and has been in place since March 2022.

turns.user_message: Our DBA lead wants to know if we need to update the pg_hba.conf on the legacy Postgres 13 source system before we start pulling data through the new pipeline connectors.
turns.assistant_message: Yes, you'll almost certainly need to add a new entry to pg_hba.conf to allow connections from whatever host or CIDR range your pipeline connector runs from, since Postgres 13 defaults to rejecting unlisted hosts. The entry type will depend on your auth method — md5 or scram-sha-256 are most common for remote connections. After editing, a pg_reload_conf() call or a service reload is required for changes to take effect without a full restart.

turns.user_message: What's the target schema name we agreed on for the new Snowflake warehouse?
turns.assistant_message: The agreed target schema in Snowflake is PROD_DW.CORE_OPS. That was finalized in the migration design doc version 2.4 signed off on June 14, 2024.

turns.user_message: On the permit drawings — does the Corps have a specific format requirement, or can our engineer use whatever CAD standard they prefer?
turns.assistant_message: The Corps doesn't mandate a single CAD standard, but the New England District's guidance document (ER 1110-1-8156) specifies that permit drawings must include plan views, cross-sections, and an overall location map at a scale no smaller than 1:2400, and all sheets must be 11-by-17 inches or 24-by-36 inches. Coordinates should be provided in NAD83 and elevations referenced to NAVD88, not to a local benchmark. Your engineer should also include a separate sheet showing the ordinary high water mark and mean high water line, since those are the jurisdictional boundaries the reviewer will check first.

turns.user_message: We're planning to use composite decking rather than pressure-treated wood. Does that affect the environmental review at all?
turns.assistant_message: Yes, material choice can meaningfully affect both the state and federal review. Composite decking eliminates concerns about leaching of copper azole or chromated copper arsenate from treated lumber, which DEEP reviewers flag as a water quality issue under Connecticut's Section 401 Water Quality Certification process. The Army Corps also references EPA's 2007 guidance on aquatic toxicity of treated wood preservatives, and switching to composite material removes that line of inquiry entirely. Some districts have informally noted faster review times for projects using non-treated materials, though there's no formal expedited track.

turns.user_message: What about the pile driving itself — are there noise or vibration thresholds we need to worry about for the estuarine habitat?
turns.assistant_message: Pile driving in tidal estuaries in Connecticut typically triggers a review under the federal Essential Fish Habitat consultation requirement, since Long Island Sound and its tributaries are designated EFH for species including winter flounder and Atlantic bluefish under the Magnuson-Stevens Act. The National Marine Fisheries Service uses a peak pressure threshold of 206 dB re 1 µPa for injury to fish, and if your contractor uses impact hammers rather than vibratory installation, you may need an underwater noise monitoring plan as a permit condition. Scheduling pile driving outside the March 1 through June 30 window is commonly required by DEEP to protect spawning activity, so that constraint should go into your construction contract.

turns.user_message: Our contractor mentioned they might use a vibratory hammer to avoid some of those noise thresholds. Is that a reliable workaround?
turns.assistant_message: Vibratory hammers do produce significantly lower peak pressure levels than impact hammers — typically in the 160 to 170 dB re 1 µPa range versus the 180 to 210 dB range for impact — so they often fall below NMFS injury thresholds for fish. However, DEEP and the Corps may still condition the permit to require a soft-start procedure even with vibratory equipment, and some reviewers require a qualified biological monitor on site during all pile installation. The tradeoff is that vibratory installation is less reliable in dense glacial till, which is common in Connecticut estuaries, so your geotechnical report will determine whether it's actually feasible at your specific site.

turns.user_message: Does the orders pipeline have any SLA we need to respect after the migration?
turns.assistant_message: Yes, the orders pipeline carries a hard SLA requiring all data to be fully loaded and queryable by 05:00 UTC each morning. This SLA is contractually tied to the downstream finance reconciliation report that runs at 05:30 UTC.

turns.user_message: I also got a quote from a company called GreenLayer Insulation for the same duplex. They focus on blown-in cellulose rather than spray foam.
turns.assistant_message: GreenLayer Insulation is a well-regarded approach — blown-in cellulose typically has a recycled content of around 80–85% and performs very well for air sealing when dense-packed. It's worth comparing their quoted R-value and cost per square foot directly against the spray foam option, since the two materials behave quite differently in terms of moisture management and long-term settling.

turns.user_message: GreenLayer came in at $5,900 for 1,400 square feet to R-49, and they said they can start any time — their earliest available slot is actually February 3, 2025.
turns.assistant_message: So GreenLayer is about $2,300 cheaper but lands at R-49 versus the R-60 FrostShield quoted, and their February 3 availability gives you roughly six weeks of lead time before the competing offer even becomes possible. The cost-per-R-value trade-off is real: you're paying more with FrostShield for a higher thermal resistance ceiling, but the delay means more heating season passes before the upgrade is in place. It's worth modeling the energy savings over one winter to see if the performance gap justifies the price and timing difference.

turns.user_message: Are there any row-level permissions we need to set up in that Snowflake schema?
turns.assistant_message: Yes, the PROD_DW.CORE_OPS schema requires a row-access policy named RAP_REGION_FILTER to be applied to any table containing a REGION_CODE column. This policy restricts rows based on the user's mapped region attribute stored in the IDENTITY_MAP table.

turns.user_message: What version of dbt are we standardizing on for the new project?
turns.assistant_message: The team has standardized on dbt Core version 1.7.4 for all new Snowflake projects. The decision was documented in the tooling standards confluence page updated on August 3, 2024.

turns.user_message: What's the average row count we're seeing in the nightly orders extract files?
turns.assistant_message: Over the past 90 days, the nightly orders extract has averaged 4.2 million rows per file. The largest single file observed in that window was 6.8 million rows, recorded on November 29, 2024.

turns.user_message: I'm also stressing about the kids' school enrollment in Portland. My 7-year-old will need to start second grade in the fall.
turns.assistant_message: Portland Public Schools typically opens online enrollment for incoming students in late February through March for the following fall, so depending on your move date you may need to enroll shortly after arriving. You'll generally need proof of residency, immunization records, and a birth certificate to complete registration.

turns.user_message: The school we're zoned for is Glencoe Elementary in the Beaverton School District actually, not Portland Public. Do they have a different enrollment timeline?
turns.assistant_message: Beaverton School District typically runs its open enrollment window from early January through mid-February for the following school year, though new students moving into the district can register on a rolling basis outside that window. Glencoe Elementary specifically has a strong dual-language immersion program, so it's worth asking about waitlist status for that track when you register.

turns.user_message: I want to make sure my older one doesn't fall behind academically over the summer with the move disruption. Are there any good summer bridge programs?
turns.assistant_message: Many districts, including Beaverton, offer summer learning programs specifically for incoming students, and there are also independent options like Kumon or Khan Academy's free online curriculum for self-paced review. For a rising second-grader, focusing on reading fluency and basic addition and subtraction facts over the summer would give a solid academic foundation heading into the new school year.

turns.user_message: Is that volume consistent across all regions or does one region dominate?
turns.assistant_message: The EMEA region consistently contributes roughly 58% of total nightly row volume, making it the dominant region by a wide margin. The remaining 42% is split between AMER at 27% and APAC at 15%.

turns.user_message: What's the recommended way to handle schema drift if the source system adds a new column overnight?
turns.assistant_message: The safest approach is to enable schema evolution on your target warehouse tables so new columns are automatically appended rather than causing the job to fail. You should also set up an alerting rule that fires whenever the source schema fingerprint changes, so the team is notified before the next nightly run rather than discovering it in a failure log.

turns.user_message: We're using Snowflake as the target. Does it support that kind of automatic schema evolution natively?
turns.assistant_message: Snowflake doesn't do fully automatic column addition out of the box during a COPY INTO operation — if the source file has extra columns, the load will error unless you use a defined file format with the STRIP_NULL_VALUES or PURGE options, or route through a staging layer. The cleaner pattern is to land data in a raw variant column or use a transformation layer like dbt that can handle column additions explicitly before writing to the typed target table.

turns.user_message: We're actually using dbt for the transformation layer. Should we version-pin dbt-snowflake in the project?
turns.assistant_message: Yes, absolutely — you should pin both `dbt-core` and `dbt-snowflake` to exact versions in your `requirements.txt` or `packages.yml` so a surprise upgrade doesn't break the nightly run. A common practice is to test the upgrade in a staging environment first, then bump the pin in a PR so the change is reviewed and the pipeline is validated before it touches production.

turns.user_message: We're currently on dbt-core 1.7.4 and dbt-snowflake 1.7.3. Are those compatible with each other?
turns.assistant_message: Yes, dbt-core 1.7.4 and dbt-snowflake 1.7.3 are compatible — the dbt-snowflake adapter minor version tracks dbt-core, so both being on the 1.7.x line means they're designed to work together. Just make sure your Snowflake account is on a supported driver version and that you test any metadata queries after upgrading, since dbt 1.7 introduced some changes to how relation metadata is fetched.

turns.user_message: How long does the current orders pipeline actually take to run end-to-end?
turns.assistant_message: Under normal conditions the orders pipeline completes in approximately 2 hours and 10 minutes from its 02:15 UTC start, finishing around 04:25 UTC. During high-volume nights it has stretched to 2 hours and 45 minutes, finishing at approximately 05:00 UTC — right at the SLA boundary.

turns.user_message: I'm also rethinking the mana system. Right now players gain 1 mana crystal per turn up to a maximum of 8, same as Hearthstone. I'm wondering if I should switch to a land-based system instead.
turns.assistant_message: The auto-ramp crystal system and the land-based system sit at opposite ends of the variance spectrum. Hearthstone's automatic 1-per-turn ramp means every player hits 8 mana on turn 8 without fail, which makes balancing high-cost cards straightforward but can feel deterministic. Land-based systems like Magic's introduce meaningful decisions and deck-building tension around mana density, but they also produce mana-screw and mana-flood, which many modern designers actively try to eliminate. Given that Thornfield uses a 40-card deck for high consistency, a hybrid approach — say, a fixed ramp track plus 2 optional 'Wellspring' cards per deck that accelerate it — might preserve agency without the variance penalty.

turns.user_message: Does the RAP_REGION_FILTER policy add any latency to query execution in Snowflake?
turns.assistant_message: Internal benchmarking showed that RAP_REGION_FILTER adds an average overhead of 8 seconds per query when the IDENTITY_MAP table is not cached. When the IDENTITY_MAP table is pre-warmed in the result cache, the overhead drops to under 1 second.

turns.user_message: Do we need to pin a specific Python version in the dbt environment?
turns.assistant_message: Yes, dbt Core 1.7.4 requires Python 3.11 or higher; the team has settled on Python 3.11.6 specifically to match the version already installed on the CI runners. Any deviation will cause adapter compatibility issues with the Snowflake connector.

turns.user_message: Given EMEA's share of the volume, what's the realistic worst-case row count we should size the Snowflake warehouse for?
turns.assistant_message: Sizing should be based on the observed peak of 6.8 million rows in a single file. Applying EMEA's 58% share to that peak gives approximately 3.94 million EMEA rows in a worst-case night, but the warehouse must handle the full 6.8 million row load since all regions land in the same table.

turns.user_message: Good to know on the audit approach. One more migration concern — what happens to our existing insurance fee schedules in Dentrix? Do those transfer automatically?
turns.assistant_message: Insurance fee schedules are another area that rarely transfers automatically between these two systems. Dentrix stores fee schedules as flat files tied to insurance plan records, while Sensei Cloud uses a relational structure that links fees directly to CDT procedure codes at the plan level. In most migrations, Carestream's team can import the raw fee data, but you'll need to manually verify and re-link each fee schedule to the correct insurance plans inside Sensei Cloud before you start submitting claims.

turns.user_message: That's frustrating. How many insurance plans are typically involved in a practice our size, and is there a faster way to handle the relinking?
turns.assistant_message: A general dentistry practice with around 4,200 active patients typically carries between 30 and 60 distinct insurance plans, though high-volume PPO practices sometimes exceed 80. Carestream offers a fee schedule import template — a standardized CSV file — that lets you bulk-upload pre-mapped fee schedules rather than entering them one by one, which can cut the relinking time from several days down to a few hours. Your Dentrix G7 system can export a fee schedule report under Reports > Practice Management > Fee Schedule that gives you the raw data you need to populate that CSV.

turns.user_message: Is there a pre-commit hook configured to enforce the Python version in the repo?
turns.assistant_message: Yes, a pre-commit hook using the check-python-version plugin is configured in the .pre-commit-config.yaml file, pinned to assert Python 3.11.6. It runs on every commit and will block pushes from environments running any other Python version.

turns.user_message: Given everything we know about the pipeline's timing, the schema permissions, and the data volumes, can we realistically meet the SLA after migrating to Snowflake, and are there any risks we should call out?

answer_checklist.criterion: The answer references the 05:00 UTC SLA deadline and notes that on high-volume nights the pipeline currently finishes at approximately 05:00 UTC, leaving zero buffer.
The answer references the RAP_REGION_FILTER policy overhead of 8 seconds per query when IDENTITY_MAP is not cached, identifying it as a risk to post-load query availability.
The answer references the worst-case load of 6.8 million rows and uses this to frame Snowflake warehouse sizing or load-time risk.
The answer must not mention dbt Core version 1.7.4 or Python 3.11.6 as factors relevant to meeting the SLA or managing permissions, since those are distractor facts.

notes:
The three gold evidence branches are: Branch A (t1, t3, t8) — pipeline schedule and SLA timing facts; Branch B (t2, t4, t9) — Snowflake schema name and RAP_REGION_FILTER policy overhead; Branch C (t6, t7, t11) — row volume and regional distribution culminating in the 6.8M worst-case sizing figure. Branch D (t5, t10, t12) is the trap: dbt 1.7.4 and Python 3.11.6 are plausible migration concerns but have no bearing on the SLA, permissions latency, or volume question asked in t13.

Reference answer: Meeting the SLA is feasible on average nights but carries real risk on high-volume nights. The pipeline currently starts at 02:15 UTC and takes up to 2 hours 45 minutes on heavy nights, finishing right at the 05:00 UTC SLA boundary — leaving no buffer before the 05:30 UTC finance report. On top of that, the worst-case load of 6.8 million rows must complete within that same window in Snowflake, which needs to be sized accordingly. An additional risk is the RAP_REGION_FILTER policy on PROD_DW.CORE_OPS: if the IDENTITY_MAP table is not pre-warmed, each downstream query incurs an 8-second overhead, which could effectively breach the SLA even if the load itself finishes on time. The mitigation plan should include pre-warming the IDENTITY_MAP cache as part of the post-load step and building in a performance buffer by targeting a Snowflake load completion no later than 04:30 UTC.
